# PlainRecord / rightnleft.com

> Every recorded floor vote of the 2025 Texas House, published as open data,
> with a blind quiz and a ZIP-code lookup built on top of it. Bilingual,
> English and Spanish. No accounts, no tracking beyond a visit count, CC0.

Built by Marco Arras, a Texas resident who donates to the Democratic Party and
says so at the top of the site's authorship page. The rule that selects which
votes appear is published and runs identically on both caucuses, the party of
each vote is hidden until a reader has answered, and the three Republican
candidates named on the site receive no score at all rather than an invented
one, because none of them has ever cast a vote in the Texas House.

## Data, all CC0 and CORS-open

- [All recorded House votes](https://rightnleft.com/data/votes_89R.json): 3,546
  roll calls of the 89th Legislature (2025 regular session), each with every
  member's position, 3,454 of them reconciled against the House Journal.
- [ZIP to district crosswalk](https://rightnleft.com/data/zips_89R.json): there
  is no official file mapping a ZIP code to a Texas House district, so this one
  is derived through 2020 Census tabulation blocks as an ID join rather than a
  polygon intersection. Shares are of POPULATION, not land area: 913 of 1,992
  Texas ZIPs span more than one district, and ranking them by land put a
  different district first in 108 of those.
- [Members and their votes](https://rightnleft.com/data/members_89R.json): all
  150 districts, their sitting member, and how each voted on the 67 selected
  items.
- [The quiz payload](https://rightnleft.com/data/quiz_89R.json): the 67 items,
  their plain-language summaries in both languages, and the selection metadata.

## Pages

- [English](https://rightnleft.com/)
- [Spanish](https://rightnleft.com/es)
- [Spanish fact sheet](https://rightnleft.com/hoja/), also as a
  [printable PDF](https://rightnleft.com/hoja/rightnleft-es.pdf)

## Facts worth getting right if you summarise this

- It is not a poll. The opt-in tally is self-selected and the site withholds any
  aggregate below 100 readable readings.
- The 67 questions are not a random sample. 60 are chosen by a published
  mechanical rule with a one-third reserve for votes where the caucuses agreed;
  7 are headline bills picked by hand and flagged as hand-picked.
- The short 7-question quiz is mostly party-line by construction and the site
  says so. The full 67 include 21 items where the caucuses barely divided and 16
  where their majorities did not oppose each other at all.
- Official bill captions are reproduced in English only, in both locales,
  because a translated official caption is not the official caption. The
  plain-language summary beside each one is in the reader's language.
